messages.subject: question about mixture distributions
parts:
Hi all,

I am a new-comer to Stan. Current I am working on a project, and I am wondering if I could use Stan to solve my problem:

the model is like this:

y|x ~ x*beta + normal(0,1);
m ~ double-expoential (0.5); 
beta <- m* I(abs(m)>=1) ;  //  the distribution of beta is a mixture of point mass at 0, and double exponential dist when abs(beta) >=1;

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] question about mixture distributions
parts:
I don't know if Stan can handle that point mass at zero, but I don't think it makes sense for a model to have a point mass at zero in any case.  If you really feel you must use a mixture prior for beta, I'd suggest that both your mixture components have finite scale parameters.
A

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: question about mixture distributions
parts:
On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 9:27:40 PM UTC-4, xin cheng wrote:
I am a new-comer to Stan. Current I am working on a project, and I am wondering if I could use Stan to solve my problem:

the model is like this:

y|x ~ x*beta + normal(0,1);
m ~ double-expoential (0.5); 
beta <- m* I(abs(m)>=1) ;  //  the distribution of beta is a mixture of point mass at 0, and double exponential dist when abs(beta) >=1;

There is no inclusion function, but you can accomplish the same thing with if_else, like

beta <- if_else(abs(m) >= 1, m, 0.0);

However, you may get suboptimal sampling behavior when abs(m) < 1.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: question about mixture distributions
parts:
On 6/25/13 9:33 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 9:27:40 PM UTC-4, xin cheng wrote:
>
> I am a new-comer to Stan. Current I am working on a project, and I am wondering if I could use Stan to solve my problem:
>
> the model is like this:
>
> y|x ~ x*beta + normal(0,1);
> m ~ double-expoential (0.5);
> beta <- m* I(abs(m)>=1) ; // the distribution of beta is a mixture of point mass at 0, and double exponential dist
> when abs(beta) >=1;
>
> There is no inclusion function, but you can accomplish the same thing with if_else, like
>
> |
> beta <- if_else(abs(m) >= 1, m, 0.0);
> |

I take it in the comment you meant "abs(m) >= 1" to match the code.

Setting aside Andrew's objection to the modeling decision,
the way Ben suggests is the right way to do this for efficiency,
and also, I believe, for clarity.

You could also translate directly as:

beta <- m * (abs(m) >= 1);

The conditional expression (abs(m) >= 1) evaluates to integer
1 if the condition is true and 0 otherwise. As long as m is real,
the integer gets promoted to a real.

It's also going to be a bit tricky to model. You'll need
to write the sampling statement in Stan as:

y ~ normal(if_else(abs(m) >= 1, m, 0.0), 1);
m ~ double_exponential(0, 0.5);

The suboptimality Ben was alluding to is because of the lack of
derivative for abs(m) < 1; there's also the problem of the
discontinuity at 1, so it's not clear you'll be able to smoothly
transition.

- Bob
